query: best stability running shoes for flat feet

factors.label: Publish structured specs
factors.desc: A machine-readable spec sheet: stack, drop, support tech, widths, price.
factors.why: AI agents lift clean, structured facts straight into their reasoning. When a shoe's specs live only in marketing prose, or hidden in code an agent does not parse, there is little concrete for it to compare against rivals. A clear, legible spec sheet gives the agent something to quote.
actions: Publish a visible spec table: stack height, heel-to-toe drop, support tech, weight, widths, price.
Mirror the same facts in schema.org Product markup, but keep them visible too (agents read visible text on a live fetch, not hidden JSON-LD).
Keep the specs current to the model actually on sale, not a retired version.

factors.label: Surface reviews & durability
factors.desc: Real owner reviews and the standout, lab-tested durability record.
factors.why: Social proof moves agents measurably: a controlled study found review-volume cues lift Claude's recommendation rate 15 to 22 percent, and agents favor recent reviews and a high rating. 361's real durability record (reviewers call it built like a tank) and owner ratings are strong, but barely surfaced where the agents read.
actions: Run sustained, verified post-purchase review collection across 3+ platforms (Amazon, Zappos, REI), never fabricated.
Seed each new model with a disclosed wear-tester program so it is not review-less at launch.
Surface the real, lab-tested durability result as a concrete, quotable stat.

factors.label: Earn third-party expert authority
factors.desc: An independent lab score (Doctors of Running: 88.8%, 9.5/10 stability).
factors.why: This is the single biggest lever we measured. A credible independent lab score flips a brand from "its own marketing claim" to "a fact the model repeats." In our experiment, surfacing Doctors of Running's real score (88.8%, 9.5 of 10 for stability) is what carried 361 from rank 6, invisible, to rank 1.6, recommended 60 percent of the time, on real agents. Specs and reviews barely moved it alone.
actions: Earn independent reviews from the labs agents trust (RunRepeat, Doctors of Running, Road Trail Run) by seeding samples of the current model.
Get a published lab score on the shoe that is actually on sale, not a retired one.
Pursue 2 to 3 corroborating lab scores so the result reads as consensus, not a one-off.

factors.label: Build community proof (Reddit)
factors.desc: Be recommended in the running communities the agents read most.
factors.why: Reddit is both baked into the agents' training data (OpenAI and Google licensed it) and the single most-cited live source, appearing in roughly 40 percent of AI answers. Fitness and footwear are among the most Reddit-anchored topics, so a brand real runners discuss for a clear use case gets pulled into recommendations.
actions: Run a disclosed brand presence and AMAs in r/RunningShoeGeeks and r/running, answering fit and sizing honestly.
Seed an honest, FTC-disclosed wear-tester program so real runners post genuine experiences (never sockpuppets).
Earn placement in community 'best of' wikis by being genuinely best for a niche, such as wide or flat feet.

factors.label: Get into editorial best-of lists
factors.desc: Earn named picks in the roundups the agents quote.
factors.why: When an agent answers 'best stability shoe', the best-of roundup is often the literal document it ranks from. The Princeton GEO study found citing reliable third-party sources is the single largest visibility lever (about +40 percent), and third-party content is cited around three times more than a brand's own pages.
actions: Get into the data-driven test pipelines agents trust (RunRepeat, OutdoorGearLab, RTINGS) by seeding the current model.
Pitch gear editors at Runner's World, Outside and Wirecutter for named, categorized picks ('best for X').
Aim for multiple outlets: cross-source corroboration compounds citation odds roughly 2.8 times.

factors.label: Publish head-to-head comparisons
factors.desc: Frame yourself against the category leader, honestly.
factors.why: Comparison content is the most-cited format (32 to 41 percent of citations), and a controlled study (CORE) showed comparison-reasoning framing promotes a product to the top pick in 77 to 85 percent of cases. ChatGPT and Claude respond most strongly to it.
actions: Publish honest, two-sided 'vs the leader' pages at the model level (e.g. vs the Brooks Adrenaline) with a real spec table.
Concede where the competitor wins; two-sided comparisons read as trustworthy and survive fact-checking.
Seed the same matchup on Reddit and review sites so it is corroborated off your own domain.
